A1.justification: Despite the changed title and formatting, both PDFs describe the same TD-GFN framework and principal experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Hypergrid, antimicrobial-peptide and molecular-design experiments in Section 4, with ablations, additional evaluations and resource measurements in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds larger-Hypergrid, pruning-sensitivity, training-objective and trajectory-quality results in Appendices D and E.

M1.justification: The core rebalancing, adversarial edge-reward extraction, pruning and prioritized backward-sampling procedures remain unchanged. V2 generalizes Algorithm 1's presentation and evaluates trajectory-balance training, whose compatibility was already stated in v1 Appendix D.5. These additions do not establish a redesigned TD-GFN method.

E1.justification: V2 adds a larger, sparser 20^4 Hypergrid scenario and datasets with uniformly reconstructed or rule-based trajectories sharing the original terminal states. These extend environment and trajectory-quality coverage within Hypergrid; the original Hypergrid, peptide and molecular-design tasks remain.

E2.justification: Molecule Design Table 1 adds Oracle-GFN, which trains using the oracle as its reward proxy, and Behavior-GFN, the data-generating policy. It also adds a Dataset reference row. The original comparator rows remain, and the TD-CQL comparison already included CQL and Dataset-GFN in v1.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols sweep K=5,7,9, compare FM and TB objectives, and hold terminal states fixed while varying trajectories. Main metrics, backbones and principal sample counts remain. Separately, v2 changes the stated K-selection criterion from retained expert to recorded transitions and describes the molecular data generator as moderately rather than well trained; these revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds pruning-threshold sensitivity, larger-grid robustness, empirical FM-versus-TB compatibility testing and a controlled analysis of trajectory structure with terminal states held fixed. These substantially expand the questions tested beyond v1's retained component ablations, scarcity tests and CQL/quantile-matching analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 0,1,2 and report means with standard deviations. Both retain the best-performing-seed exception for molecular CQL and IQL results. V2 extends the same uncertainty-display convention to additional figures without introducing new statistical procedures or increased run counts.

E6.justification: V2 adds Oracle-GFN, Behavior-GFN and Dataset scores plus results for larger grids, K sensitivity, TB training and reconstructed trajectories. Table 1 retains TD-GFN's top-10 reward of 7.733±0.036 and adds Oracle-GFN's 7.718±0.014. New analyses show TB overfitting on Bad data and poorer distribution fitting with uniform paths on Expert, Mixed and Median data. Section 4.1 also corrects all-mode discovery from fewer than 500 to fewer than 5,000 visits while retaining the corresponding plot.

T1.justification: V2 adds an explicit pruned-graph TB loss and associated probability and normalizer definitions in Equation 9; v1 only stated TB compatibility. Existing Equations 1–8 are retained, with the FM equation moved to Appendix D.7. No new proofs appear. The new equation's sum over all graph edges makes its stated per-trajectory dependence unclear.

C1.justification: The central proxy-free training contribution remains. V2 adds the headline claim of matching or slightly surpassing Oracle-GFN with 20 times fewer training trajectories and more explicitly claims that indirect guidance prevents learned-reward error propagation. These extend the performance comparison and strengthen the robustness claim.

C2.justification: Appendix E expands substantially beyond v1's adversarial-training and deterministic-environment limitations. V2 discusses dependence on informative trajectory structure, possible failure with noise-only trajectories, reasons for using GFlowNet-generated datasets, hypotheses explaining Oracle-GFN comparisons, and applicability to cyclic and continuous settings. It also adds online-training and softer-guidance directions while retaining the original limitations.

D1.justification: V2 specifies uniform and rule-based trajectory reconstruction, explains recovery of peptide trajectories from terminal sequences, identifies the provided peptide proxy, and documents fixing the TB backward policy to Equation 7. The architecture and hyperparameter tables, hardware, resource measurements and COFlowNet access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially expands positioning against closely related work. V2 acknowledges the shared edge-importance insight with Silva et al.'s Weighted Detailed Balance and explains methodological differences and complementarity. It also discusses KL-weakFM, additional offline-training approaches and supporting trajectory-data literature. Naming RO-GFlowNets and updating publication metadata do not themselves constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution bullets are substantially rewritten around indirect guidance and proxy-error propagation. V2 reorganizes method exposition, moves the FM formulation into the training-objective appendix and replaces the short Future Directions section with thematic Discussions. The title, affiliation block and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the pipeline diagram, adds an introductory reward-versus-convergence plot, expands Table 1 and introduces figures for larger grids, K sensitivity, TB training and trajectory quality. It also revises the Hypergrid visualization and broadly reformats page layout. Retained benchmark and ablation figures are distinguishable from these additions despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: V1 already provided substantial benchmark and ablation evidence. V2 strengthens it through controlled trajectory-quality tests, threshold sensitivity and more informative molecule baselines, while better explaining applicability limits. These gains are tempered by the unclear new TB equation and the headline 20-fold efficiency claim, whereas Table 1 implies approximately 16-fold. With the original FM evidence preserved, the revision provides a useful but limited net quality improvement.
